The agent shall create a file named `case_120.inp` in the working directory containing the exact content provided in the Input deck code block, character-for-character, with no modifications to any node coordinates, element connectivity, boundary conditions, material definitions, nsets, transforms, or step block.
The agent shall then execute CalculiX in the working directory using the command `ccx -i case_120` first, falling back to `ccx case_120` if the first form is not recognized by the installed version.
The agent shall determine the run outcome by reading `case_120.sta`; the status is "success" only if the file contains the line "JOB COMPLETED", otherwise the status is "error".
The agent shall capture the CalculiX version string by running `ccx -v` (or the closest equivalent such as `ccx --version` or reading the banner from the run output) and store it verbatim.
The agent shall write a file named `results.json` in the working directory containing a JSON object with the keys solver (value "calculix"), case_id (value "case_120"), status (value "success" or "error" as determined above), ccx_version (the captured version string), artifacts (an array listing filenames of any output files produced such as case_120.sta, case_120.cvg, case_120.dat, case_120.frd, case_120.sta), and notes.
In the notes field the agent shall record the exact shell command used to invoke ccx.
If the status is "error", the notes field must additionally include the error message text and the name of the file (e.g. case_120.sta or the ccx stdout/stderr) from which the failure was diagnosed.
The agent shall not alter any physics definitions in the input deck, shall not add or remove nodes, elements, loads, boundary conditions, or step controls.
The reference text containing displacement, force, and stress values is informational only and shall not be incorporated into the input file or used to modify the deck.
